record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: Dualities for graded quivers with adjoints
record.original_question: Study dualities for m-graded quivers in the presence of adjoint fields.

evidence.quote: Question 19. Study the dualities for graded quivers involving adjoint fields.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be an $m$-graded quiver with potential, by which is meant a finite quiver whose arrows carry a $\mathbb{Z}/(m+1)$-grading (with arrows of degree $c$ and $m+1-c$ paired by orientation reversal) together with a superpotential of total degree $m$. Such data encode a quiver gauge theory associated to a Calabi–Yau $(m+2)$-fold, whose order-$(m+1)$ Seiberg-like dualities are realized by mutations of $Q$ at nodes that carry no adjoint fields (i.e., no loops at the mutated node).

An adjoint field at a node $i$ is an arrow from $i$ to itself (of some degree $c \in \{1,\dots,m\}$), together with its conjugate partner determined by the grading.

Problem. Develop a theory of order-$(m+1)$ dualities (equivalently, mutation rules for the underlying $m$-graded quivers with potential) at nodes that carry one or more adjoint fields. Specifically:

(a) Define a mutation operation $\mu_i$ on an $m$-graded quiver with potential $(Q,W)$ at a node $i$ possessing adjoint fields of arbitrary degrees, producing a new $m$-graded quiver with potential $(Q',W')$ that:
  (i) reduces to the standard mutation when $i$ has no adjoints;
  (ii) is compatible with the underlying Calabi–Yau $(m+2)$-fold geometry; and
  (iii) reproduces, for $m=1$, Kutasov–Schwimmer-type dualities of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories with adjoint matter.

(b) Determine the conditions on the degrees and superpotential couplings of the adjoint fields under which such a mutation is well defined, and describe the resulting transformation of ranks, arrows, and superpotential terms.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that mutations of $m$-graded quivers (equivalently, order-$(m+1)$ dualities) are currently formulated only at nodes without adjoint fields/loops, both in the physics and the higher cluster category literature. Treatment of nodes with adjoints remains incomplete; recent works on Kutasov–Schwimmer-type dualities for graded quivers (e.g., 2024 preprints) explicitly revisit this case but do not provide a complete general framework, so the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: On the Classification of Duality Webs for Graded Quivers
status_evidence.snippet: Mutations of m-graded quivers correspond to order-(m+1) Seiberg-like dualities, formulated at nodes without adjoint fields.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art restricts mutations to nodes without adjoints/loops.

status_evidence.title: Deconfinements, Kutasov–Schwimmer dualities and graded quivers
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work revisits dualities involving adjoint matter in the graded quiver setting via deconfinement techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists but a complete mutation rule for nodes with adjoints is not given.

status_evidence.title: Higher cluster categories and QFT dualities
status_evidence.snippet: Higher cluster category mutations correspond to graded quiver dualities, with adjoint/loop cases noted as incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Mathematical mutation theory likewise excludes nodes with loops.
